instrument: PianoCraft Grand (piano), horn, trumpet, trombone, tuba, flute, oboe, clarinet, strings, celesta, crotales and vibraphone
corpus: University of Iowa Electronic Music Studios, Musical Instrument Samples (MIS)
license: Public: "may be downloaded and used for any projects, without restrictions" (https://theremin.music.uiowa.edu/MIS.html, read 2026-11-02)
usage: Analysis and fitted synthesis constants only (src/engine); raw audio stays in calibration/ (git-ignored) and is never bundled or played

sources.recording: Steinway & Sons model B, Evan Mazunik, 5 and 27 November 2001, 2017 Voxman Music Building, Michael Cash; Neumann KM 84s 8 inches above the centre of the bass and of the treble strings (left, right), Mackie 1402-VLZ, Panasonic SV-3800 DAT, 16-bit 44.1 kHz stereo, not anechoic; by label pp Bb0-C8 (87), mf B0-C8 less Gb7 (85), ff A0-C8 (88), each note held to its decay. Several labels are wrong, by pitch (a harmonic sieve in the bass, the fundamental's peak against the other dynamics in the treble): ff's A0 holds A#0 and its A#0 and B0 more takes of C1; pp's C1 holds B0; mf's G7-C8 hold F#7-B7. tools/pianos.py maps them, leaving ff without A0 and B0, pp without C1 and mf without C8
French horn, Jessica Wiskus, 27 July 1997, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; pp, mf, ff chromatic runs (pp lacks C2-B3, mf lacks C3-B3)
B-flat trumpet (Bach 180S37 Stradivarius), Aren Van Houzen, 16 May 2003, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; without vibrato, pp, mf, ff, E3-E-flat 6
Tenor trombone, 27 July 1997, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; pp, mf, ff, E2-C5

CC tuba (Mirafone 1865U), David Spies, November 2003, anechoic chamber, Earthworks at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono (from 96 kHz); pp, mf, ff, C1-C4. Recorded quietly: harmonics more than 45 dB under the strongest, or above 3 kHz, are left out of the fit
Flute, Sonja Feig, April 2000, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; without vibrato, pp, mf, ff, B3-D-flat 7
Oboe (Howarth S5), Kira Wharton, 23 July 1997, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; pp, mf, ff, B-flat 3-A-flat 6
B-flat clarinet (Buffet R13), Christine Bellomy, 3 August 1998, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; pp, mf, ff, D3-C7
Violin, Josue Jean-Francois, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; arco by string, pp, mf, ff, G3-B7
Viola, Charletta Taylor, 2 March 1996, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; arco by string, pp, mf, ff, C3-B-flat 6
Cello (Stradivarius copy), Jean Montes, 16 November 2001, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; arco by string, pp, mf, ff, C2-B-flat 5
Double bass (Wurlitzer), Alison Mann, 20 November 2001, anechoic chamber, Neumann KM 84 at 5 feet, 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono; arco by string, pp, mf, ff, E1-G4
Crotales, Andrew Thierauf, 29 March 2013, anechoic chamber, Earthworks QTC40 at 5 feet, 24-bit 44.1 kHz stereo; one stroke per disc, pp and ff, C6-C8. The set is tuned about 17 cents above A = 440

Orchestra bells (steel bars), plastic mallets, Andrew Thierauf, 10 June 2013, anechoic chamber, Earthworks QTC40 at 5 feet, 24-bit 44.1 kHz stereo; one stroke per bar, pp, mf, ff, C5-E8. For the celesta's bars: there is no celesta in the collection

Vibraphone ("sustain": pedal down; the motor off, as measured: no tremolo in any fundamental; mallets not stated), Andrew Thierauf, 10 June 2013, anechoic chamber, Earthworks QTC40 at 5 feet, 24-bit 44.1 kHz stereo; one stroke per bar, pp, mf, ff, C3-F6 (some pp and mf runs too faint to split). The set is tuned about 10 cents above A = 440
